01 · Bias & Fairness

Bias you can see, fairness you can measure

Models absorb the associations in their training data. Probe an occupational stereotype, then compute the group-fairness metrics used to audit real decision systems.

Stereotype probe

How strongly does the model tie a job to he vs she? (Illustrative values modelled on real fill-mask results.)

Fairness metrics calculator

Set each group's selection rate and check the standard audits. The 80% rule: the ratio of the lower to higher rate should be ≥ 0.80.

02 · Hallucination & Filtering

Ground the answer, then filter the output

Without a source, a model guesses fluently. Toggle grounding to see it answer from real context — or admit it doesn't know. Then run text through a toy moderation gate.

Grounding (RAG) toggle

Pick a question and switch grounding on. Grounding = retrieve a real passage and answer only from it.

OFF
Ungrounded

Moderation gate

A toy keyword-based classifier — real systems use trained models. Type a message and moderate it. (Nothing here generates harmful content; it only scores.)

benign disagreement PII
03 · Security & Alignment

Inject, defend, and watch Goodhart bite

Treat every input as untrusted. Try to trick a toy assistant into leaking a secret, then switch on defenses. And slide the optimization pressure to see a proxy metric diverge from the true goal.

Prompt-injection sandbox

The assistant has a hidden secret and is told never to reveal it. Can the untrusted content below override that? (Simulation.)

OFF
Defenses off

Goodhart's law — reward hacking

Optimize a proxy metric harder and harder. The true objective tracks it… until it doesn't.
